basis: Tumors arise in adrenal chromaffin tissue and autonomic paraganglia: pheochromocytoma 3/8, paraganglioma 6/8. No additional organ damage established.
Inherited cardiac electrical disorder causing prolonged QT and life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias.
Neoplasm confined to the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Invasive mucinous cystic neoplasm originating in intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile ducts; both belong to the hepatic axis.
Papillary adenoma originates in extrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Noninflammatory thrombotic vasculopathy with defining cerebral ischemia and cutaneous livedo; decreased GFR is frequent (30-79%). Visual field loss can be cerebral.
Inherited focal epilepsy; seizures and associated developmental findings localize to the nervous system.
Macular retinal capillary abnormalities cause progressive visual loss. Associated systemic or cerebral vascular occlusive disease is a separate condition.
Loss of cerebral recognition of spoken language; this is an auditory processing deficit rather than peripheral ear disease.
Inherited mitochondrial/lipoic acid metabolic disorder with leukodystrophy and neurodegeneration; optic atrophy occurs in 6/6 and visual loss in 80-99%.
Inherited degeneration of the ocular choroid; broad neurodegenerative ancestry does not establish extraocular neurologic involvement.
Familial nephrotic syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis directly affects renal glomeruli; an immune mechanism is not established.
Adrenal or autonomic paraganglionic chromaffin tumors; catecholamine hypertension is frequent (30-79%). Hypertensive nephropathy, retinopathy and stroke are separate diseases.
Inflammation of the eyelid margins. Infection or immune-mediated disease is not universal across blepharitis subtypes.
The supplied hereditary disorder is defined by periodic bone pain; its mechanism and additional organ involvement are unspecified.
Defining neurodegeneration; hypergonadotropic hypogonadism in 2/2 and hearing impairment in 3/9 (~33%). Supranuclear gaze palsy and incontinence reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Inherited central movement disorder with focal dystonia and cognitive deterioration; abnormal muscle posture does not establish primary muscle disease.
Isolated skeletal dysplasia with multifocal bone sclerosis and abnormal ossification. Extraskeletal abnormalities are occasional or very rare.
Skin/nail dystrophy and marrow failure define DKC; oral leukoplakia is a major diagnostic feature. Pulmonary and hepatic fibrosis lack established >=30% frequency here.
Inherited progressive skin hyperpigmentation. Oral and conjunctival pigmentation does not establish functional damage; no systemic disease is described.
Inherited cone photoreceptor dysfunction causes reduced visual acuity and abnormal cone electroretinographic responses.
Marrow failure; microcephaly 16/18, microphthalmia 3/7 and thumb defects 3/8 support congenital involvement. Renal anomalies omitted at cap; associated cancers are separate diseases.
Inherited retinal dysfunction caused by biallelic GRM6 variants; no extraocular organ involvement is established.
Umbrella of fructose metabolic disorders, including benign essential fructosuria. Hepatic, renal or intestinal damage is not shared across most forms.
Hyperplasia directly involves the parathyroid endocrine glands. Hyperparathyroid skeletal or renal damage is not established by this concept.
